title: Edit Discovery in Human-AI Interactions
abstract: arXiv:2610.22661v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human-AI interactions are becoming a rich source of data for improving AI systems: while many model responses are already satisfactory, others expose failures that could become valuable supervision if identified and corrected. We study this setting through the notion of an editor: a more capable evaluation process that can inspect a response and either confirm it or modify it, but whose invocation is costly. The editor may be a human expert, a stronger AI system, or the same model equipped with additional computation, context, tools, or information. The key challenge is to decide which interactions to send to the editor before knowing whether an edit will actually be made, since invoking the editor itself consumes limited resources such as expert time, inference cost, latency, or tool-use overhead. We formulate this problem as Edit Discovery Optimization (EDO), which seeks to minimize edit opportunities missed among skipped interactions

translated_title: 人机交互中的编辑发现
translated_abstract: 人机交互正在成为改进AI系统的丰富数据来源：虽然许多模型响应已经令人满意，但其他响应所暴露的失败若能被识别并纠正，可能成为宝贵的监督信号。我们通过“编辑器”的概念来研究这一场景：编辑器是一种能力更强的评估过程，它能够检查响应并对其予以确认或修改，但调用它的成本高昂。编辑器可以是人类专家、更强大的AI系统，或者是配备了额外计算、上下文、工具或信息的同一模型。关键挑战在于，在尚不知道是否真的会发生编辑的情况下，就要决定将哪些交互发送给编辑器，因为调用编辑器本身会消耗有限的资源，例如专家时间、推理成本、延迟或工具使用开销。我们将此问题形式化为编辑发现优化，其目标是最小化在被跳过的交互中错过的编辑机会。
tldr: 提出编辑发现优化（EDO）框架，通过在不知晓是否会产生编辑的情况下智能选择将哪些人机交互发送给成本高昂的编辑器（如人类专家或更强AI），以最小化错过的编辑机会并节约有限资源。
en_tdlr: Proposes Edit Discovery Optimization (EDO), a framework that intelligently selects which human-AI interactions to send to a costly editor (such as a human expert or stronger AI) without knowing whether an edit will actually occur, aiming to minimize missed edit opportunities while conserving limited resources.
